relations.subject: William Carey
relations.evidence: William Carey (17 August 1761 – 9 June 1834) was an English Christian missionary... who founded the Serampore College and the Serampore University

relations.subject: William Carey
relations.evidence: who founded the Serampore College and the Serampore University, the first degree-awarding university in India

relations.subject: William Carey
relations.evidence: The same year, the Governor-General founded Fort William College, a college intended to educate civil servants. He offered Carey the position of professor of Bengali.

relations.subject: William Carey
relations.evidence: One of his colleagues was his Munshi, Ram Ram Basu who taught him Sanskrit and other Indian languages.

relations.subject: William Carey
relations.evidence: In May 1799 William Ward and Hannah and Joshua Marshman arrived from England and joined Carey in his work. The three men became known as the Serampore trio.

relations.subject: William Carey
relations.evidence: In 1820 Carey founded the Agri Horticultural Society of India at Alipore, Calcutta, supporting his enthusiasm for botany.
